completes_w3_row_reason: the level's own counters are measured; its reuse share against libc is not measurable with this instrument

reuse_share_unmeasurable.why: memhook.c watches sqlite3_mem_methods, and the memsys5 heap never crosses it
evidence: speedtest1.c:3218 pHeap = malloc(nHeap), a plain libc malloc before the work
speedtest1.c:3220 sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_HEAP, pHeap, ...) installs memsys5 over it
speedtest1.c:3475 free(pHeap), after all of it
the memsys5 arm's report carries no libc level at all, so level 0 recorded nothing
the shipped arm's report carries hook_alloc[libc] = 1801880, so the instrument does record that level when the mem methods are the default
reuse_share_unmeasurable.what_the_source_shows: one allocation before the work and one release after all of it, so every memsys5 reuse necessarily precedes the release. That is read off the workload's source, not measured.
reuse_share_unmeasurable.what_would_measure_it: interposing the malloc family, which the APR and memcached wirings do and memhook.c does not
